description: We are AstroVitalis, a team passionate about software development, AI, and data science. We aim to build a health monitoring application that helps astronauts track and understand their health during long-duration space missions. Our goal is to support astronaut health and safety through technology and innovation.
summary:
EMBERA is a fire intelligence platform that brings NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations together to help users explore where and when thermal hotspots are detected. It harmonizes qualified historical observations on a shared spatial grid and matched observation days, applying a sensor calibration only when regional overlap and validation support comparison. Interactive maps, timelines, seasonal baselines, and country-level views help users examine activity while keeping raw sensor detections distinct from the harmonized activity index.
EMBERA also provides statistical anomaly analysis against historical seasonal patterns and a trained novelty model evaluated on held-out years. These signals describe unusual observed activity; they do not predict future fires or confirm that a hotspot is a wildfire. Recent near-real-time observations are presented separately because their calibration transfer has not been validated. By making data provenance, coverage, uncertainty, and comparison methods visible, EMBERA helps people interpret satellite fire observations more responsibly and supports informed monitoring and follow-up.
details:
EMBERA is an interactive fire activity atlas that helps users explore NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS thermal hotspot observations across time. Its backend processes the supplied historical archive into daily spatial grids, applies confidence and vegetation filters, and aligns MODIS Aqua and VIIRS NOAA-20 observations on dates when both sensors reported detections. Where regional overlap supports a validated conversion, the platform calibrates VIIRS occupancy against MODIS and presents a harmonized activity index alongside the separate raw sensor counts. Interactive maps, timelines, seasonal charts, and country-level views make these comparisons easier to explore.

EMBERA also calculates historical seasonal baselines and robust statistical anomaly scores, and includes a trained novelty model evaluated on chronological validation and holdout periods. The dashboard presents these results as analysis of observed activity—not as fire prediction or confirmation. Recent NRT observations are ingested and displayed separately from historical harmonized results. The platform was built with Python, FastAPI, SQLite, Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Leaflet. Its design emphasizes traceable observations, clear sensor distinctions, and transparent interpretation of satellite hotspot data.
projectRefs: NASA FIRMS datasets (historical archive and supplied MODIS/VIIRS files)
